statement: For every nonzero rational number $p$ (an element of the unnormalised rationals $\mathbb{Q}^{\mathrm{u}}$, i.e. fractions with integer numerator and positive denominator, compared by the usual equality $\simeq$ of rational values), taking the reciprocal twice returns the original value: $\frac{1}{1/p} \simeq p$. Equivalently, the reciprocal map $p \mapsto 1/p$ is an involution on the nonzero rationals.
